items.title: Oliver Nelson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 10, 2020
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] In our collection at the college I have a score your dad did for Joe Williams... [INTERVIEWEE] I think in Hollywood he was afraid not to take offers.

ctx.x: Well it’s interesting, he would think of those when they had to go on a record. But I’ve got a ton of scores of N-201s and 302s and that kind of, and I have to sit down and figure out a lot of times what they were. And some of this stuff has never been done. And I’ve got boxes and boxes of music and I’ve had one of my students kind of help me catalogue stuff but then Covid came around so she can’t even come to the house anymore. But most of the stuff he had a good name for. That book of eleven songs, he had one…

In our collection at the college I have a score your dad did for Joe Williams, and so nothing seemed to faze him. I wonder, did he seem compelled to take every offer given to him? © Fillius Jazz Archive -10-

I think in Hollywood he was afraid not to take offers. Because my stepmother would always say, you know, we’ve got enough money, you don’t have to work anymore. But I think his point was out of sight, out of mind. So you kind of had to keep the system rolling there as far as doing stuff, and that didn’t help him. Plus he wouldn’t go to the doctor. All the reports you probably read say he died of a heart attack but he didn’t die of a heart attack at all. He died from pancreatitis and metamorphosis of the liver,…
